## Three rules

1. **Check every output you use.** Numbers, code and references produced by a model can be wrong while looking right.
2. **Know what you are sharing.** Unpublished data, proposals under review and other people's manuscripts may not be yours to upload.
3. **Keep a record.** Save prompts, model names and dates with your analysis, as you would for any instrument setting.

## Minimal setup

- **A frontier chat model** for reading, writing and reasoning tasks. Free models are not up to the task, at least in 2026.
- **A coding agent** for anything that touches code or data: it runs and tests what it writes.
- **Your usual tools**: ADS, arXiv or PubMed, Python and the libraries of your field. The material in the [Library](../../library.qmd) plugs models into these rather than replacing them.

## What models are good at, and what not

Good at, with checking:

- explaining a method or a paper from outside your field, at the level you ask for;
- turning your notes or outline into clear text, and shortening text that is too long;
- writing, translating and testing code, from a one-off plot to a refactor of an old pipeline;
- reading a set of papers you give them and comparing what they say;
- acting as a demanding first reader of a draft or a proposal.

Not good at, or not without help:

- being the source of facts, measured values or references: they produce plausible ones from memory;
- anything published after their training, unless they can search;
- arithmetic done "in their head": ask them to write and run code instead;
- judging what matters most in a field: they repeat what is written most often.

## Chat, agent or API

A **chat** interface (in the browser or an app) is enough for reading and writing. A **coding agent** works in a folder on your computer or on a server: it reads files, runs commands and checks its own results, which makes it the right tool for code and data, and also the one that needs most care ([Coding agents for data analysis](../AIG0004-coding-agents-data-analysis/index.qmd)). The **API** is for running the same task many times from a script, for example classifying a thousand abstracts.

Ask your institution whether it has an agreement with a provider. Institutional accounts usually exclude your data from training and are the safe choice for unpublished material.
